2
Which row shows a quantity and an incorrect unit?
quantity
unit
A
efficiency
no unit
B
moment of force
N m–1
C
momentum
N s
D
work done
J

hints: Look at what each quantity is calculated from: efficiency from a ratio of energies, moment from force times distance, momentum from mass times velocity, work from force times distance.
Recall that multiplying or dividing units follows the equation: $\text{N} \times \text{m}$ is different from $\text{N} / \text{m}$, and $\text{N} \times \text{s}$ is the same as $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$.
Check which listed unit cannot be made by combining the base units of its defining equation, especially the unit written with $\text{m}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Identify the defining equation for each quantity: efficiency $= \text{useful energy out} / \text{total energy in}$, moment $= Fd$, momentum $= mv = Ft$, work done $= Fd$.

Deduce the expected unit: a ratio of the same quantity has no unit, $F \times d$ gives $\text{N m}$, $mv$ gives $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$ which also equals $\text{N s}$, and work gives $\text{N m}$ which is defined as $\text{J}$.
Compare with the table: no unit for efficiency is correct, $\text{N s}$ for momentum is correct, and $\text{J}$ for work done is correct.
The moment of force should be $\text{N m}$, but the table shows $\text{N m}^{-1}$. That is force divided by length and would suit a quantity like spring constant, not a moment.
Therefore the quantity with an incorrect unit is the moment of force. This is option B.

A.explanation: Efficiency is $\text{useful output} / \text{total input}$ for the same type of energy or power, so the units cancel and no unit is correct.

B.explanation: Moment of force is $F \times d$, so its unit is $\text{N m}$, not $\text{N m}^{-1}$ which means newton divided by metre.

C.explanation: Momentum equals impulse $Ft$, so $\text{N s}$ is equivalent to $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$ and is a correct unit.

D.explanation: Work done is force times distance in the direction of the force, whose SI unit is the joule $\text{J}$.
